# Query catalogue with outputs

**Owner: Vismay.** Rubric item 7 (joins, nested, correlated and recursive queries), the CTE/window/function part of item 8, views (006) and RBAC (item 12). Generated by `npm run docs:queries` on 2026-10-29 from the seeded database, run as the commissioner through `civic_admin`. Seed timestamps are relative to "now", so counts shift slightly between runs.

The SQL is the same text the **DB Lab** page (`/admin/db-lab`) runs and the files in [`db/queries/`](../../db/queries/) contain.

## 1. Complaint full detail (5-way join)

**Concept:** INNER + LEFT JOIN across five tables · **Rubric:** 7 · Join queries · **File:** [`db/queries/01-join-full-detail.sql`](../../db/queries/01-join-full-detail.sql)

Every open complaint with its category, department, ward, filer and assignee. LEFT JOIN keeps unassigned complaints.

```sql
SELECT c.complaint_id, c.title, cat.category_name, d.department_name,
       w.ward_name, filer.name AS filed_by, staff.name AS assigned_to, c.status
FROM complaint c
JOIN complaint_category cat ON cat.category_id = c.category_id
JOIN department d           ON d.department_id = c.department_id
JOIN ward w                 ON w.ward_id = c.ward_id
JOIN app_user filer         ON filer.user_id = c.filed_by
LEFT JOIN app_user staff    ON staff.user_id = c.assigned_to
WHERE c.status IN ('OPEN','ASSIGNED','IN_PROGRESS','REOPENED','ESCALATED')
ORDER BY c.created_at DESC
LIMIT 15;
```

## 2. Departments including those with no open work

**Concept:** LEFT JOIN + COUNT with FILTER · **Rubric:** 7 · Join queries · **File:** [`db/queries/02-left-join-zero.sql`](../../db/queries/02-left-join-zero.sql)

LEFT JOIN keeps departments that have zero matching complaints, which an INNER JOIN would drop.

```sql
SELECT d.department_name,
       COUNT(c.complaint_id) FILTER (WHERE c.status IN ('OPEN','ASSIGNED','IN_PROGRESS','REOPENED','ESCALATED')) AS open_now,
       COUNT(c.complaint_id) AS all_time
FROM department d
LEFT JOIN complaint c ON c.department_id = d.department_id
GROUP BY d.department_id, d.department_name
ORDER BY open_now DESC;
```

Output (7 rows):

| department_name | open_now | all_time |
|---|---|---|
| Roads & Infrastructure | 13 | 39 |
| Water Supply & Sewerage | 13 | 38 |
| Parks & Urban Forestry | 4 | 15 |
| Street Lighting | 4 | 26 |
| Solid Waste Management | 3 | 15 |
| Public Health | 2 | 21 |
| Storm Water Drains | 2 | 22 |

## 3. Confirmed duplicate pairs (self-join)

**Concept:** Self-join on complaint via duplicate_of · **Rubric:** 7 · Join queries · **File:** [`db/queries/03-self-join-duplicates.sql`](../../db/queries/03-self-join-duplicates.sql)

The complaint table joined to itself: each duplicate next to the original it was merged into.

```sql
SELECT dup.complaint_id AS duplicate_id, dup.title AS duplicate_title,
       orig.complaint_id AS original_id, orig.title AS original_title,
       dm.similarity_score
FROM complaint dup
JOIN complaint orig ON orig.complaint_id = dup.duplicate_of
JOIN duplicate_match dm ON dm.complaint_id = dup.complaint_id
                       AND dm.matched_complaint_id = orig.complaint_id
ORDER BY dm.similarity_score DESC;
```

Output (5 rows):

| duplicate_id | duplicate_title | original_id | original_title | similarity_score |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 169 | Footpath tiles missing near 27th Main | 26 | Broken footpath slabs at 27th Main | 0.93 |
| 175 | Stray dog pack chasing vehicles at 80 Feet Road | 67 | Injured stray dog near 80 Feet Road | 0.90 |
| 167 | Park lights and benches damaged at Hebbal flyover | 5 | Broken swings in park near Hebbal flyover | 0.80 |
| 171 | Exposed live wire near Sony World junction | 30 | Electric cable hanging low at Sony World junction | 0.80 |
| 165 | Drinking water leaking onto the road at 11th Main | 3 | Water pipe burst at 11th Main | 0.79 |

## 4. Field staff with no open assignments

**Concept:** Anti-join with NOT EXISTS · **Rubric:** 7 · Nested queries · **File:** [`db/queries/04-anti-join-idle-staff.sql`](../../db/queries/04-anti-join-idle-staff.sql)

Staff for whom no open complaint exists. Useful for rebalancing load.

```sql
SELECT u.user_id, u.name, d.department_name, w.ward_name
FROM app_user u
JOIN department d ON d.department_id = u.department_id
JOIN ward w ON w.ward_id = u.ward_id
WHERE u.role = 'STAFF' AND u.is_active
  AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM complaint c
                  WHERE c.assigned_to = u.user_id
                    AND c.status IN ('OPEN','ASSIGNED','IN_PROGRESS','REOPENED','ESCALATED'))
ORDER BY d.department_name, u.name;
```

## 5. Wards with more open complaints than the city average

**Concept:** Nested subquery in HAVING · **Rubric:** 7 · Nested queries · **File:** [`db/queries/05-nested-wards-above-avg.sql`](../../db/queries/05-nested-wards-above-avg.sql)

The inner query computes the average open count per ward; the outer query keeps wards above it.

```sql
SELECT w.ward_name, COUNT(*) AS open_complaints
FROM complaint c
JOIN ward w ON w.ward_id = c.ward_id
WHERE c.status IN ('OPEN','ASSIGNED','IN_PROGRESS','REOPENED','ESCALATED')
GROUP BY w.ward_id, w.ward_name
HAVING COUNT(*) > (
  SELECT AVG(cnt) FROM (
    SELECT COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM complaint
    WHERE status IN ('OPEN','ASSIGNED','IN_PROGRESS','REOPENED','ESCALATED')
    GROUP BY ward_id) per_ward)
ORDER BY open_complaints DESC;
```

Output (3 rows):

| ward_name | open_complaints |
|---|---|
| Koramangala | 10 |
| Jayanagar | 6 |
| Basavanagudi | 5 |

## 6. Resolved slower than their own department's average

**Concept:** Correlated subquery · **Rubric:** 7 · Correlated queries · **File:** [`db/queries/06-correlated-slower-than-dept.sql`](../../db/queries/06-correlated-slower-than-dept.sql)

The inner AVG is recomputed for each outer row's department, which makes the subquery correlated.

```sql
SELECT c.complaint_id, c.title, d.department_name,
       ROUND(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM c.resolved_at - c.created_at) / 3600, 1) AS hours_taken
FROM complaint c
JOIN department d USING (department_id)
WHERE c.resolved_at IS NOT NULL
  AND c.resolved_at - c.created_at > (
        SELECT AVG(c2.resolved_at - c2.created_at)
        FROM complaint c2
        WHERE c2.department_id = c.department_id
          AND c2.resolved_at IS NOT NULL)
ORDER BY hours_taken DESC
LIMIT 15;
```

Output (15 rows, first 10 shown):

| complaint_id | title | department_name | hours_taken |
|---|---|---|---|
| 17 | Park lights and benches damaged at 100 Feet Road | Parks & Urban Forestry | 331.9 |
| 140 | Injured stray dog near Gandhi Bazaar | Public Health | 203.6 |
| 32 | Stray dog pack chasing vehicles at 14th Main | Public Health | 201.9 |
| 135 | Stray dog pack chasing vehicles at Domlur flyover | Public Health | 170.6 |
| 138 | Deep pothole near 11th Main | Roads & Infrastructure | 156.1 |
| 145 | Large crater on the road at 5th Block bus stop | Roads & Infrastructure | 154.6 |
| 121 | Large crater on the road at 5th Block bus stop | Roads & Infrastructure | 140.6 |

| 49 | Road surface caved in near 5th Block bus stop | Roads & Infrastructure | 122.4 |
| 31 | Broken swings in park near 80 Feet Road | Parks & Urban Forestry | 114.6 |

## 7. Departments with more than 3 complaints past SLA

**Concept:** GROUP BY + HAVING + aggregate · **Rubric:** 6 · DML / aggregates · **File:** [`db/queries/07-group-having-breached.sql`](../../db/queries/07-group-having-breached.sql)

Open complaints whose deadline has passed, grouped by department, keeping only the worst offenders.

```sql
SELECT d.department_name, COUNT(*) AS breached,
       ROUND(AVG(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM now() - c.sla_deadline) / 3600), 1) AS avg_hours_overdue
FROM complaint c
JOIN department d USING (department_id)
WHERE c.status IN ('OPEN','ASSIGNED','IN_PROGRESS','REOPENED','ESCALATED')
  AND c.sla_deadline < now()
GROUP BY d.department_name
HAVING COUNT(*) > 3
ORDER BY breached DESC;
```

Output (3 rows):

| department_name | breached | avg_hours_overdue |
|---|---|---|
| Roads & Infrastructure | 12 | 594.7 |
| Water Supply & Sewerage | 10 | 443.9 |
| Parks & Urban Forestry | 4 | 122.5 |

## 8. Complaints escalated twice or more

**Concept:** Correlated EXISTS with aggregate · **Rubric:** 7 · Correlated queries · **File:** [`db/queries/08-exists-repeat-escalations.sql`](../../db/queries/08-exists-repeat-escalations.sql)

EXISTS runs once per complaint row and checks its own escalation count.

```sql
SELECT c.complaint_id, c.title, w.ward_name, c.status
FROM complaint c
JOIN ward w USING (ward_id)
WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM escalation e
              WHERE e.complaint_id = c.complaint_id
              GROUP BY e.complaint_id
              HAVING COUNT(*) >= 2)
ORDER BY c.complaint_id;
```

## 9. Escalation path for every field staff member

**Concept:** WITH RECURSIVE over supervisor_id · **Rubric:** 8 · CTE / recursive · **File:** [`db/queries/09-recursive-supervisor-chain.sql`](../../db/queries/09-recursive-supervisor-chain.sql)

Walks supervisor_id upward: staff → department head → commissioner. This is the chain fn_escalation_target uses.

```sql
WITH RECURSIVE chain AS (
  SELECT u.user_id AS staff_id, u.user_id, u.name, u.role, u.supervisor_id, 0 AS depth
  FROM app_user u WHERE u.role = 'STAFF' AND u.ward_id = 1
  UNION ALL
  SELECT ch.staff_id, s.user_id, s.name, s.role, s.supervisor_id, ch.depth + 1
  FROM app_user s JOIN chain ch ON s.user_id = ch.supervisor_id
)
SELECT staff_id, depth, name, role FROM chain
ORDER BY staff_id, depth;
```

## 10. Duplicate chains resolved to their root complaint

**Concept:** WITH RECURSIVE + CYCLE clause · **Rubric:** 8 · CTE / recursive · **File:** [`db/queries/10-recursive-duplicate-chain.sql`](../../db/queries/10-recursive-duplicate-chain.sql)

Follows duplicate_of until it reaches the canonical complaint; CYCLE guards against loops.

```sql
WITH RECURSIVE chain AS (
  SELECT complaint_id AS start_id, complaint_id, duplicate_of, 0 AS depth
  FROM complaint WHERE duplicate_of IS NOT NULL
  UNION ALL
  SELECT ch.start_id, c.complaint_id, c.duplicate_of, ch.depth + 1
  FROM complaint c JOIN chain ch ON c.complaint_id = ch.duplicate_of
) CYCLE complaint_id SET is_cycle USING path
SELECT start_id, complaint_id AS root_id, depth
FROM chain WHERE duplicate_of IS NULL
ORDER BY start_id;
```

Output (5 rows):

| start_id | root_id | depth |
|---|---|---|
| 165 | 3 | 1 |
| 167 | 5 | 1 |
| 169 | 26 | 1 |
| 171 | 30 | 1 |
| 175 | 67 | 1 |

## 11. Filed vs resolved per day, last 14 days

**Concept:** Recursive CTE generating a calendar · **Rubric:** 8 · CTE / recursive · **File:** [`db/queries/11-recursive-date-series.sql`](../../db/queries/11-recursive-date-series.sql)

A recursive CTE produces every day, so quiet days show 0 instead of disappearing.

```sql
WITH RECURSIVE days AS (
  SELECT (current_date - 13) AS day
  UNION ALL
  SELECT day + 1 FROM days WHERE day < current_date
)
SELECT d.day,
       (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM complaint c WHERE c.created_at::date = d.day) AS filed,
       (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM complaint c WHERE c.resolved_at::date = d.day) AS resolved
FROM days d
ORDER BY d.day;
```

Output (14 rows, first 10 shown):

| day | filed | resolved |
|---|---|---|
| 2026-10-15 18:30 | 6 | 1 |
| 2026-10-16 18:30 | 1 | 3 |
| 2026-10-17 18:30 | 1 | 3 |
| 2026-10-18 18:30 | 5 | 1 |
| 2026-10-19 18:30 | 5 | 2 |
| 2026-10-20 18:30 | 4 | 3 |
| 2026-10-21 18:30 | 3 | 4 |
| 2026-10-22 18:30 | 5 | 5 |
| 2026-10-23 18:30 | 2 | 2 |

## 12. Ward SLA ranking with window functions

**Concept:** Multiple CTEs + RANK() + running total · **Rubric:** 8 · CTE / window · **File:** [`db/queries/12-window-ward-ranking.sql`](../../db/queries/12-window-ward-ranking.sql)

CTEs compute per-ward resolution stats; RANK() orders wards by SLA compliance and SUM() OVER builds a running total.

```sql
WITH resolved AS (
  SELECT ward_id, resolved_at <= sla_deadline AS met
  FROM complaint WHERE resolved_at IS NOT NULL AND status <> 'DUPLICATE'
), per_ward AS (
  SELECT w.ward_name, COUNT(*) AS resolved,
         ROUND(100.0 * AVG(met::int), 1) AS sla_met_pct
  FROM resolved r JOIN ward w USING (ward_id)
  GROUP BY w.ward_name
)
SELECT RANK() OVER (ORDER BY sla_met_pct DESC) AS rank,
       ward_name, resolved, sla_met_pct,
       SUM(resolved) OVER (ORDER BY sla_met_pct DESC) AS running_resolved
FROM per_ward
ORDER BY rank;
```

Output (10 rows):

| rank | ward_name | resolved | sla_met_pct | running_resolved |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Rajajinagar | 13 | 84.6 | 13 |
| 2 | Koramangala | 34 | 82.4 | 47 |
| 3 | HSR Layout | 9 | 77.8 | 65 |
| 3 | Jayanagar | 9 | 77.8 | 65 |
| 5 | Hebbal | 13 | 76.9 | 78 |
| 6 | BTM Layout | 10 | 70.0 | 88 |
| 7 | Basavanagudi | 6 | 66.7 | 94 |

## 13. SLA compliance by department (stored function)

**Concept:** Calling fn_sla_compliance(dept, from, to) · **Rubric:** 8 · Function · **File:** [`db/queries/13-fn-sla-compliance.sql`](../../db/queries/13-fn-sla-compliance.sql)

A PL/pgSQL function returns the share of complaints resolved within SLA for a department and date range.

```sql
SELECT d.department_name,
       fn_sla_compliance(d.department_id, now() - interval '90 days', now()) AS sla_met_pct
FROM department d
ORDER BY sla_met_pct DESC NULLS LAST;
```

| Storm Water Drains | 75.0 |

## 14. Full-text search: "water leak"

**Concept:** tsvector @@ websearch_to_tsquery + ts_rank · **Rubric:** 8 · Full-text search · **File:** [`db/queries/14-fts-keyword.sql`](../../db/queries/14-fts-keyword.sql)

Keyword search over the generated search_tsv column with a GIN index. Compare with semantic search in the Vector Console.

```sql
SELECT complaint_id, title,
       ROUND(ts_rank(search_tsv, q)::numeric, 3) AS rank
FROM complaint, websearch_to_tsquery('english', 'water leak') AS q
WHERE search_tsv @@ q
ORDER BY rank DESC
LIMIT 10;
```

## 17. Escalation chains (view)

**Concept:** vw_escalation_chain · joins escalation, policy and the user directory · **Rubric:** 8 · View · **File:** [`db/queries/17-view-escalation-chain.sql`](../../db/queries/17-view-escalation-chain.sql)

Every escalation step with who it came from and who it went to. Level 1 goes to the department head, 2 to the ward admin, 3 to the commissioner.

```sql
SELECT complaint_id, escalation_level, level_label,
       escalated_from_name, escalated_to_name, escalated_to_role, still_open
FROM vw_escalation_chain
ORDER BY complaint_id DESC, escalation_level
LIMIT 20;
```

## 19. RBAC: privilege matrix per database role

**Concept:** has_table_privilege / has_any_column_privilege over pg_class · **Rubric:** 12 · RBAC in the database · **File:** [`db/queries/19-rbac-privilege-matrix.sql`](../../db/queries/19-rbac-privilege-matrix.sql)

What each of the four group roles may do on every table and view, read live from the catalog. (cols) means a column-level GRANT, finer than the table.

```sql
WITH roles(role) AS (
  VALUES ('civic_anon'), ('civic_citizen'), ('civic_staff'), ('civic_admin')
), privs AS (
  SELECT c.relname, r.role,
         concat_ws(', ',
           CASE WHEN has_table_privilege(r.role, c.oid, 'SELECT') THEN 'SELECT'
                WHEN has_any_column_privilege(r.role, c.oid, 'SELECT') THEN 'SELECT(cols)' END,
           CASE WHEN has_table_privilege(r.role, c.oid, 'INSERT') THEN 'INSERT'
                WHEN has_any_column_privilege(r.role, c.oid, 'INSERT') THEN 'INSERT(cols)' END,
           CASE WHEN has_table_privilege(r.role, c.oid, 'UPDATE') THEN 'UPDATE'
                WHEN has_any_column_privilege(r.role, c.oid, 'UPDATE') THEN 'UPDATE(cols)' END,
           CASE WHEN has_table_privilege(r.role, c.oid, 'DELETE') THEN 'DELETE' END) AS granted
  FROM pg_class c
  JOIN pg_namespace n ON n.oid = c.relnamespace
  CROSS JOIN roles r
  WHERE n.nspname = 'public' AND c.relkind IN ('r', 'v', 'm') AND c.relname <> 'schema_migrations'
)
SELECT relname AS object,
       coalesce(nullif(max(granted) FILTER (WHERE role = 'civic_anon'), ''), '–')    AS anon,
       coalesce(nullif(max(granted) FILTER (WHERE role = 'civic_citizen'), ''), '–') AS citizen,
       coalesce(nullif(max(granted) FILTER (WHERE role = 'civic_staff'), ''), '–')   AS staff,
       coalesce(nullif(max(granted) FILTER (WHERE role = 'civic_admin'), ''), '–')   AS admin
FROM privs
GROUP BY relname
ORDER BY relname;
```

Output (25 rows, first 10 shown):

| object | anon | citizen | staff | admin |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| app_user | SELECT(cols) | SELECT(cols) | SELECT(cols) | SELECT(cols), INSERT(cols), UPDATE(cols) |
| complaint | SELECT(cols) | SELECT, INSERT(cols) | SELECT, UPDATE(cols) | SELECT, UPDATE(cols) |
| complaint_category | SELECT | SELECT | SELECT | SELECT |
| department | SELECT | SELECT | SELECT | SELECT |
| duplicate_match | – | SELECT | SELECT, UPDATE(cols) | SELECT, UPDATE(cols) |
| escalation | SELECT(cols) | SELECT | SELECT | SELECT |
| escalation_policy | SELECT | SELECT | SELECT | SELECT |
| mv_public_ward_stats | SELECT | SELECT | SELECT | SELECT |
| notification | – | SELECT, UPDATE(cols) | SELECT, UPDATE(cols) | SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE(cols) |
| status_history | – | SELECT | SELECT | SELECT, INSERT |

## 20. RBAC: row-level security policies

**Concept:** pg_policies catalog view · **Rubric:** 12 · RBAC in the database · **File:** [`db/queries/20-rbac-rls-policies.sql`](../../db/queries/20-rbac-rls-policies.sql)

Every RLS policy: the table, the command it guards, the roles it applies to and its USING expression. Rows with no matching policy are invisible (default deny).

```sql
SELECT tablename, policyname, cmd, roles,
       left(regexp_replace(coalesce(qual, with_check), 's+', ' ', 'g'), 110) AS rule
FROM pg_policies
WHERE schemaname = 'public'
ORDER BY tablename, policyname;
```
